title: Manipur Cabinet Approves ₹4,000 Monthly Assistance for Eligible PhD Scholars
summary: Manipur Cabinet approves ₹4,000 monthly assistance for eligible PhD scholars for up to three years, supporting 50 new researchers annually.
body:
Imphal, November 25, 2026: The Manipur Cabinet has approved a financial assistance scheme providing ₹4,000 per month to eligible PhD scholars pursuing research in higher educational institutions across the state, aiming to support young researchers and promote higher education.

The decision was taken during a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh on Wednesday.

Under the Manipur Chief Minister’s Financial Assistance Scheme for Research Work in Higher Educational Institutions, eligible PhD scholars who do not receive any regular fellowship or salary will be entitled to ₹4,000 monthly assistance for a period of up to three years.

The scheme will support up to 50 new scholars annually.

*Eligible Institutions*

The financial assistance will cover eligible PhD scholars from the following institutions:

- Dhanamanjuri University

- Manipur Technical University

- Manipur University of Culture

*Colleges affiliated with Manipur University*

The initiative is expected to provide financial support to researchers pursuing doctoral studies and encourage research activities in higher educational institutions across Manipur.

**Cabinet Approves Other Developmental Measures**

During the same meeting, the Cabinet also gave in-principle approval for the establishment of divisional taxation offices at Jiribam, Senapati, Moreh and Imphal to provide taxation-related services and guidance closer to traders and businesses.

The Cabinet further approved the contractual recruitment of 162 staff, including lecturers, for six newly established District Institutes of Education and Training (DIETs) at Heirok, Kangpokpi, Pherzawl, Noney, Kasom Khullen and Moreh.

The buildings of the institutes are reportedly ready, and the recruitment is expected to facilitate their functioning. The annual expenditure for the state is estimated at approximately ₹1.69 crore, with the Centre sharing part of the cost.

The Cabinet meeting was attended by Deputy Chief Ministers Nemcha Kipgen, who joined virtually, and Losii Dikho, Home Minister Govindas Konthoujam, Art and Culture Minister Kh. Loken Singh, Chief Secretary, administrative secretaries and other officials.

The Chief Minister said the Cabinet deliberated on various matters concerning public welfare programmes and developmental activities and took decisions aimed at the welfare and development of the state.
author: Mirror Lilong Desk
